stem: A crop block develops interveinal chlorosis on older leaves while root-zone EC has risen across several irrigations. Tissue results are not yet available. Which next step best strengthens the nutrient differential?
choices: Diagnose magnesium deficiency from leaf color alone.
Ignore root-zone history because visual symptoms identify nutrient causes.
Increase every fertilizer element at the next irrigation.
Compare root-zone EC, pH, moisture trend and matched unaffected plants before deciding whether nutrient supply, uptake or water balance best fits the evidence.
rationale: Nutrient-related symptoms can overlap with root-zone and water-balance problems. Comparing root-zone trends and unaffected plants strengthens the differential without treating leaf appearance as proof of one deficiency.
